subject: Several questions + error with Part 4 Reporting

messages.author: 5ea25187985f565f
messages.subject: Several questions + error with Part 4 Reporting
parts:
Hi Vincent,

First - thanks for the fantastic work with the GGIR package. I'm having a couple of issues and I'm hoping you can point me in the right direction.

1. I'm getting the following error when running the g.shell.GGIR script for the part 4 report:

Report part 4
 loading all the milestone data from part 4 this can take a few minutes
Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, i, (cnt + 1), value = NaN) :
  subscript out of bounds
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)

The warnings look like:
1: In `[<-.factor`(`*tmp*`, iseq, value = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0,  ... :
  invalid factor level, NA generated

I've attached the script as a text file in case I've made a mistake. The output from part 4 is a series of rows with "NA", presumably due to the warning.

2. The script attached produces summary data which in most cases looks like reasonable estimates. Due to a mistake, some of the geneactivs were left on the chargers after they were initialised, meaning that they have differing start times depending on when they came off the charger. This does funny things to the estimates. Is there some way in GGIR to set a "solid" start time (i.e., a date/time to start from)? The hrs.del.start/end are based on time from when they were initialised. 

3. In addition to the full day summaries, I'd like to have estimates for specific periods of the day (e.g., before school, during school, etc). I understand this would mean repeatedly processing the data, which is fine. Can I just check - the variable I would manipulate to do this is qwindow? Does the L5M5 window need to be changed?

4. In addition to the above, I could have the script loop part 2 for the filters and change the location that it writes to. Is there a more elegant solution than this?


Again, appreciate any advice you can give.

Kind regards,
Taren

messages.author: d17553208d13f6a8
messages.subject: Re: Several questions + error with Part 4 Reporting
parts:
Hi Taren, hope you're well. 

I was just posting another thread and thought I'd send you a quick reply based on what I know in relation to your 4th point: for specific periods of the day use the qwindows [so 9,3.5 could represent the school day for example]. If you use the ilevels to specify your intensity cutpoints, the output will provide minutes in the intensities for the period specified in the qwindows line. This is something we have recently been doing with some of our data.

Hope this is of some help - good luck with your study.

cheers,
Stuart

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Several questions + error with Part 4 Reporting
parts:
Hi Taren,

1. Can you inspect the pdfs that are generated and stored in subfolder meta/sleep.qc/... Do these make sense to you? For example, do you count the expected number of nights, and is the sustained inactivity indicator (bottom colored line) up when you would expect it? Secondly, can you check whether the error occurs for all your datasets and files or just for one specific file or dataset? If yes, try to verify what makes that dataset different.

2. If you always expect a specific number of days of measurement then you could try variable 'strategy =  3' with ndayswindow specified. I developed this for a study where they sent the accelerometer by mail to the participant without knowing exactly when the participant would start wearing the monitor. If that doesn't work for your study design then split your dataset in subsets such that each subset has more or less the same number of non-wear hours at the beginning of the measurement. Inspecting the pdf plots produced by part 2 may help you here. Next, process each subset with strategy =2 and hrs.del.start set specific to that subset.

3. See response by Stuart... also note that all the epoch by epoch values are stored in the RData milestone data. So, if you or someone around you is a bit familiar with R you can extract this information yourself. IMP$metashort as produced by part2 has all the epoch by epoch acceleration values.

4. To some extend the code facilitates sensitivity analyses to a variety of parameters, but I did not facilitate this for all parameters assuming that for most of them people do not even want to run sensitivity analyses. To do this there are currently two options: (1) Run the analyses multiple times with different parameter settings and make a copy of the intermediate outputs. (2) Make a copy of the entire output folder after you have run part1 and then run part 2, 3 and/or 4 for each copy of the output separately. To do this make sure that the various copies of the output folder have a name that starts with 'output_' followed by an informative description xx about what you intended to do with them. Next, set argument studyname to xx and make sure that xx matches the xx in "output_xx". Also, set argument datadir to c(). In that way the code will consider each copy of the output folder as a separate study, named xx.

Vincent
